'''Justin Michael Reed''' (January 16, 1982 – October 20, 2017)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/reedju01.html|title=Justin Reed Stats - Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 21, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://m.msnewsnow.com/story/36642421/former-ole-miss-nba-star-justin-reed-dies-of-cancer|title=Former Ole Miss, NBA star Justin Reed dies of cancer|website=m.msnewsnow.com|access-date=October 21, 2017}}</ref> was an American professional [[basketball]] player, who played at the [[small forward]] position.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Celtics forward Justin Reed passes away from cancer |url=https://247sports.com/nba/boston-celtics/article/former-celtics-forward-justin-reed-passes-away-after-battling-cancer-109178746/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Reed led the [[University of Mississippi]]'s [[Ole Miss Rebels]] as part of the "Provine Posse", three former [[Provine High School]] teammates (along with [[Aaron Harper (basketball)|Aaron Harper]] and [[David Sanders (basketball)|David Sanders]]) who played together for the Rebels.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Morales |first=Antonio |title=Former Ole Miss standout and Provine alumnus Justin Reed dies at 35 |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2017/10/20/former-ole-miss-standout-and-provine-alumnus-justin-reed-dies-35/783440001/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=The Clarion-Ledger |language=en-US}}</ref>

Under the tutelage of 2001 Naismith Coach of the Year [[Rod Barnes]], Reed became an all-around player and a dominant force in the [[Southeastern Conference]]. An All-SEC selection in each of his four years at The University of Mississippi, Reed led the team both on the court and in the locker room.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Davis |date=2017-10-20 |title=Former Ole Miss basketball star Justin Reed dies after battle with cancer |url=https://oxfordeagle.com/2017/10/20/former-ole-miss-basketball-star-justin-reed-dies-battle-cancer/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=The Oxford Eagle |language=en}}</ref> As a freshman, Reed guided the Rebels through two [[NCAA]] tournament wins en route to a first ever "Sweet Sixteen" appearance for the Ole Miss program in 2001.<ref name=":0" />

==NBA career==
Following his successful career as a forward at the [[University of Mississippi]], Reed was selected in the second round (40th overall) by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. Following one and one-half seasons with little playing time, he was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on January 26, 2006, in a multi-player deal; he enjoyed a successful 40 games with the Timberwolves and, at season's end, became a restricted [[free agent]]. Minnesota then rewarded him with a three-year contract worth $4,310,500.<ref>[http://hoopshype.com/salaries/houston.htm NBA Salaries - Houston Rockets] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315075730/http://hoopshype.com/salaries/houston.htm |date=March 15, 2015 }}, HoopsHype.com; accessed October 21, 2017.</ref>

On June 14, 2007, it was officially announced that Reed and teammate [[Mike James (basketball, born 1975)|Mike James]] would be traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], for [[Juwan Howard]].<ref name=rocketstrade>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2903593 Wolves, Rockets agree to Howard-James trade]; ESPN.com, June 14, 2007.</ref> He was subsequently waived by the Rockets without having appeared in a single game for them.

==Death==
Reed died from [[angiosarcoma]], a cancer of the vasculature, on October 20, 2017.<ref name=msn>{{cite web |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/former-celtic-passes-away-at-35-years-old/ar-AAtM5gE |title=Former Celtic Passes Away at 35 Years Old |last=Bradley |first=Logan |website=msn.com |access-date=October 20, 2017 }}</ref>
